business_profile.description: Nemeris consolidates a regional field-equipment distribution operation and a recurring maintenance-services platform, supplying utility and industrial maintenance crews with ruggedized tools, diagnostics, replacement parts, and calibration/maintenance services.

revenue_model.how_they_make_money: product sales (equipment/diagnostics/parts) plus recurring contracted maintenance and calibration services
revenue_model.recurring_vs_transactional: Mixed. Preventive maintenance plans and calibration services are recurring/contractual; ruggedized tool systems and diagnostic units are project-driven equipment shipments. Management explicitly does not treat every service dollar as contractually recurring and excludes unsupported ARR claims.
revenue_model.pricing_and_contracts: Not itemized in the IC memo beyond channel mix; equipment revenue recognized on dispatch or customer acceptance, service revenue on contracted visits/coverage.

channels.economics: Project schedules and end-customer approvals drive timing
Plant outage and maintenance cadence drive timing
Renewal, technician capacity and attachment rates

customers.profile: Utility contractors, industrial maintenance organizations, rental/distribution partners, field-service plan buyers
customers.concentration: Not quantified in the IC memo (managed via account-level review and renewal tracking; no top-customer % disclosed) — flagged draft
customers.stickiness: Mixed — maintenance plans and calibration create renewal/contractual stickiness; equipment shipments are project/backlog-driven and not assumed to convert uniformly

suppliers_and_inputs.key_inputs: Equipment and component purchases, direct field labor, freight and logistics
suppliers_and_inputs.concentration: Not disclosed in the IC memo — flagged draft
suppliers_and_inputs.cost_drivers: Freight/logistics and component sourcing costs (per Income Statement COGS breakdown); competition may compress equipment margins

business_profile.geography_footprint: Coordinated from a principal service center with regional field teams and third-party logistics support; no foreign subsidiary relied upon for collateral or cash flow in the base case — domestic operations.
business_profile.seasonality_cyclicality: Ordinary month-to-month volatility from equipment shipment/dispatch timing even where annual customer activity is stable; project timing affected by customer capital budgets, weather, permitting and labor availability.
business_profile.competitive_position: Fragmented market across equipment manufacturers, specialty distributors, service contractors and in-house teams. Competes on equipment availability, technical support, configuration expertise and service response rather than lowest price. Less purchasing leverage than large distributors (focused regional platform).

ownership.structure: Nemeris Holdings, LLC owns the borrower (Nemeris Field Systems, LLC); Nemeris Service Operations, LLC is a co-guarantor employing field personnel.

credit_thesis.pillar: Mixed product-and-service revenue model with a recurring maintenance/calibration base cushions month-to-month equipment shipment timing volatility
credit_thesis.monitored_by: Revenue mix by offering; EBITDA margin trend

credit_thesis.pillar: Modest opening leverage with a quarterly-tested 5.00x maximum Net Leverage covenant provides meaningful covenant cushion
credit_thesis.monitored_by: Net Leverage Ratio vs 5.00x cap (quarterly, from covenant compliance certificates)

credit_thesis.pillar: First-priority blanket collateral package (receivables, inventory, equipment, IP) supports recovery even though it is not relied on as primary repayment
credit_thesis.monitored_by: Collateral coverage vs funded debt (Collateral metrics box)

credit_thesis.pillar: Positive operating cash generation supports scheduled debt service without reliance on the undrawn delayed-draw tranche as a liquidity cure
credit_thesis.monitored_by: Operating cash flow; delayed-draw utilization (Debt & Liquidity tab)

key_risks_at_uw.risk: Shipment timing — monthly equipment revenue can shift materially
key_risks_at_uw.early_warning_signal: Large MoM swings in Ruggedized Tool Systems / Diagnostic Units revenue lines vs budget

key_risks_at_uw.risk: Customer concentration — loss or delay can affect revenue and receivables
key_risks_at_uw.early_warning_signal: AR concentration or DSO deterioration (note: no AR aging file is currently delivered to verify this directly)

key_risks_at_uw.risk: Inventory exposure — availability strategy can create slow-moving stock
key_risks_at_uw.early_warning_signal: Rising Inventory Days / inventory aging skew toward older buckets

key_risks_at_uw.risk: Margin pressure — competition and freight affect gross profit
key_risks_at_uw.early_warning_signal: Gross margin decline vs the 0.20 floor threshold or vs budget

key_risks_at_uw.risk: Management depth — key technical and commercial relationships matter
Forecast execution — pipeline is not equivalent to contracted backlog
key_risks_at_uw.early_warning_signal: Persistent revenue miss vs the approved budget (already observed: 2026-06 revenue -13.9% vs budget, YTD -11.8% vs budget)

key_risks_at_uw.risk: Collateral realization — specialized assets may sell below book value
key_risks_at_uw.early_warning_signal: Not monitorable monthly; noted as a structural limitation of the collateral read

our_view.thesis_status: Leverage remains well inside the 5.00x cap (1.32x at Q2 2026, corrected) and no delayed-draw reliance has occurred, so the core credit protections are intact. Revenue is running persistently below the approved budget (-13.9% in June 2026, -11.8% YTD) on shipment-timing, which is the underwriting's own named risk rather than a new one — worth tracking but not thesis-breaking at this cushion level.
our_view.what_would_change_our_mind: A shift from a shipment-timing revenue miss to a structural gross-margin or EBITDA-margin decline; any recurrence of an unsupported/prospective EBITDA add-back attempt in a certificate; or Net Leverage approaching roughly half the 5.00x cap.
